hard_cpu_time_throttling.policy: tenant-owned cgroup v2 child controlled through cpu.max; cpu.stat usage/throttled_usec returned on query
security: session must own a directly delegated tenant cgroup
generation fencing rejects stale policy transitions
CPU controller must be present and explicitly enabled in cgroup.subtree_control
unsupported or unavailable controller paths fail closed
hard_cpu_time_throttling.scheduler_bridge: faisal_sched_group_set_cpu_bandwidth()/get_cpu_bandwidth() call the upstream CFS bandwidth group implementation and are exported GPL-only

accelerator_tenant_memory_isolation.uapi: AGI_LC_ACCEL_ISOLATION_TENANT_MEMORY with accelerator registration, account, and release extensions
accelerator_tenant_memory_isolation.ownership: registered device is bound to session identity, tenant child cgroup ID, and tenant cgroup generation
accelerator_tenant_memory_isolation.accounting: device-memory account is accepted only within total device memory and reports tenant ownership and memory limit
accelerator_tenant_memory_isolation.denial: over-limit account returns EDQUOT and AGI_LC_ACCEL_ACCOUNT_STATUS_MEMORY_DENIED
accelerator_tenant_memory_isolation.hardware_scope: provider-neutral control-plane validation only; no physical GPU/NPU, VRAM, DMA, IOMMU, vendor-driver, or production accelerator qualification claimed

validation.protected_files: M63-COMPUTE-CONTEXT-DESIGN.md and M63-SECURITY-REVIEW.md remain untracked and unstaged

limitations: cpu.max enforcement is validated in a QEMU cgroup2 hierarchy, not on a production multi-socket host
reported throttled_usec was zero in the short policy smoke test; a sustained workload benchmark is still needed to quantify throttle behavior
accelerator accounting validates ownership and memory admission semantics without a physical accelerator
no claim is made that FAISAL is AGI, conscious, self-learning, or hardware-qualified solely from this milestone
